stages.title: Raw materials
stages.summary: Quartz, silver, copper, aluminum, steel, glass inputs, and specialty minerals enter the chain.

stages.title: Silicon metal and polysilicon
stages.summary: Quartz is reduced to silicon metal, then purified into solar-grade polysilicon.

stages.title: Ingots and wafers
stages.summary: Polysilicon is melted into crystal ingots and sliced into thin wafers.

stages.title: Solar cells
stages.summary: Wafers are textured, doped, coated, and metallized into electricity-producing cells.

stages.title: Module materials and assembly
stages.summary: Cells are wired, sealed between protective layers, framed, tested, and shipped as modules.

stages.title: Trackers and racking
stages.summary: Steel foundations and moving structures hold modules and follow the sun.

stages.title: Inverters and controls
stages.summary: Power electronics convert module output from direct current into grid-ready alternating current.

stages.title: Electrical balance of system
stages.summary: Cable, combiner boxes, switchgear, and transformers collect power and connect the plant to the grid.

stages.title: Installed U.S. project
stages.summary: Manufactured equipment becomes an operating U.S. solar plant and sets the annual demand for the chain.

stages.title: CdTe comparison
stages.summary: Thin semiconductor layers deposited on glass replace the polysilicon, wafer, and separate cell stages.
